t.6.99.1: While those rākṣasa women were lamenting thus, his eldest wife, beloved and stricken with grief, gazed upon her husband.
t.6.99.2: Seeing her husband Daśagrīva slain by Rāma, whose deeds are beyond imagining, Mandodarī, wretched with grief, lamented there.
t.6.99.3: Surely, O mighty-armed younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa, even Puraṃdara is afraid to stand before you when you are enraged.
t.6.99.4: Surely the sages and the brahmins, the gods on earth, the glorious Gandharvas and the Cāraṇas have fled to all the quarters out of dread of you.
t.6.99.5: You, who have been vanquished in battle by Rāma, a mere man, do you feel no shame, O king? What is this, O bull among rākṣasas?
t.6.99.7: Your destruction at the hands of Rāma in battle does not seem fitting, for you move beyond the reach of men and can take on any form at will.
t.6.99.6: How could a mere man, a wanderer in the forest, have slain you, the irresistible one, who had overrun the three worlds endowed with splendor and might?
t.6.99.8: Nor do I believe this deed of Rāma at the head of the army, that you, who were fully protected on every side, should have been assailed by it.
t.6.99.9: Having first conquered your senses, you conquered the three worlds; and now, as if remembering that old enmity, those very senses have conquered you.
t.6.99.10: Or else Vāsava himself has come in the form of Rāma, having devised an inconceivable illusion for your destruction.
t.6.99.11: For at the very moment when your brother Khara, surrounded by many rākṣasas, was slain in Janasthāna, it was clear even then that he was no mere human.
t.6.99.12: The very moment Hanumān, by his valour, entered the city of Laṅkā, hard to enter even for the gods, at that very moment we were struck with dread.
t.6.99.13: When I told you, "Let there be no conflict with Rāghava," you would not accept it; this is the fruit of that which has now arrived.
t.6.99.14: And without cause, O bull among Rākṣasas, you have come to desire Sītā, to the destruction of your sovereignty, your body, and your own people.
t.6.99.16: Neither in lineage, nor in beauty, nor in courtesy is Maithilī superior to me or even equal to me, but you, out of delusion, do not perceive it.
t.6.99.15: O evil-minded one, in violating Sītā, who is mine and who surpasses even Arundhatī and Rohiṇī, you have indeed done an unworthy deed.
t.6.99.17: For all beings, death never comes without a cause; in your case, this death had its cause made by Maithilī.
t.6.99.18: Maithilī, freed from sorrow, will take her pleasure together with Rāma, but I, whose merit is small, have fallen into a dreadful ocean of grief.
t.6.99.19: Having sported in your company on Kailāsa, on Mandara and on Meru, and likewise in the Caitraratha forest and in all the gardens of the gods,
t.6.99.20: I who used to travel in a fitting aerial chariot with incomparable splendour, wearing bright garlands and garments and gazing upon those many various lands, am now cast down from the enjoyments of desire by the slaying of you, my hero.
t.6.99.21: Truthful in speech was that illustrious brother-in-law of mine when he said, 'This destruction of the foremost of the rākṣasas has drawn near.'
t.6.99.22: Through a clinging vice born of desire and anger, you have left this entire race of Rākṣasas without a protector.
t.6.99.23: Indeed, you whose strength and valour are renowned ought not to be mourned by me; yet, owing to a woman's nature, my mind turns toward pity.
t.6.99.24: Taking with you your good deeds and your evil deeds, you have gone to your own destined end; it is myself I grieve for, stricken with sorrow by separation from you.
t.6.99.25: You who resemble a dark rain-cloud, clad in yellow garments and adorned with splendid armlets, why do you lie here bathed in blood, your limbs all flung apart? As though deep in sleep, why do you not answer me, stricken as I am with grief?
t.6.99.26: Why do you not look upon me, the daughter's daughter of a yātudhāna of great valour, skilled and never fleeing in battles?
t.6.99.28: In battle, your iron club, the smiter of foes, adorned with a network of gold, was cut into a thousand pieces by arrows and scattered.
t.6.99.27: Here is that weapon, bright as the sun and ever worshipped by you, with which you slay your enemies in battle as the wielder of the thunderbolt slays with his thunderbolt.
t.6.99.29: Shame upon this heart of mine, afflicted with grief, which does not burst into a thousand pieces now that you have met your death!
t.6.99.30: Meanwhile Rāma said to Vibhīṣaṇa: "Let the funeral rites of your brother be performed, and send these women back."
t.6.99.31: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, humble and knowing dharma, having heard those words and pondered them with his intellect, gave Rāma a reply full of dharma and sound purpose, spoken solely to accord with Rāma's wishes.
t.6.99.32: One who has abandoned his vow of righteousness, cruel, merciless and false, a violator of other men's wives: I am not fit to perform the funeral rites for such a one.
t.6.99.33: For this Rāvaṇa is my enemy in the form of a brother, devoted to the harm of all; though worthy of honor out of respect due to an elder, he does not deserve worship.
t.6.99.34: O Rāma, people on earth will call me cruel; but once they have all heard of his qualities, they will say again that it was rightly done.
t.6.99.35: Hearing that, Rāma, foremost among the upholders of dharma, was supremely pleased, and he, skilled in speech, spoke these words to Vibhīṣaṇa, who was well versed in speech.
t.6.99.36: What is dear to you must be done by me as well, for through your might victory has been won by me. Yet, O lord of the rākṣasas, I must surely tell you what is fitting.
t.6.99.37: Granted, this night-roaming demon was given to unrighteousness and falsehood; yet he was ever glorious, mighty and valiant in battles.
t.6.99.38: It is heard that the great-souled and mighty Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds cry out, was never defeated by the gods headed by Śatakratu.
t.6.99.39: Enmities end with death, and our purpose has been accomplished. Let his funeral rites be performed, for he is as much mine as he is yours.
t.6.99.40: O mighty-armed one, he deserves to receive from you without delay the funeral rite performed according to the prescribed rules; O knower of dharma, you will thereby become a sharer in glory.
t.6.99.41: Having heard the words of Rāghava, Vibhīṣaṇa, making haste, provided Rāvaṇa with funeral rites befitting him.
t.6.99.42: Vibhīṣaṇa gave the fire to him in accordance with the prescribed rites, and, speaking words of comfort again and again, he consoled those women.
t.6.99.43: And when all the Rākṣasī women had entered the city, Vibhīṣaṇa approached Rāma's side and then stood there humbly.
t.6.99.44: Rāma too, together with his army, with Sugrīva and with Lakṣmaṇa, rejoiced at having slain his enemy, as Śatakratu did after killing Vṛtra.
